results.title: 1.Dualismo Cartesiano
results.summary: Cartesian dualism posits a fundamental split between the thinking mind and the extended body, leading to the intractable problem of how these distinct substances interact. This historical framework necessitated subsequent philosophical attempts to explain the mind-body connection.
results.keywords: Dualism, Descartes, Res Cogitans, Res Extensa, Mind-Body Problem

results.title: 1.Identity Over Time
results.summary: This note summarizes the problem of identity through time and the inconsistencies between change and numerical identity. It highlights the hylomorphic solution of distinguishing between essential and accidental properties.
results.keywords: identity, change, hylomorphism, accidental properties

results.title: 10.Epifenomenalismo de Huxley
results.summary: Huxley's epifenomenalism suggests that consciousness is a non-causal byproduct of brain activity, akin to the steam from a locomotive's whistle. While this materialist view simplifies the mind-body problem, it creates a significant evolutionary puzzle regarding the purpose of consciousness.
results.keywords: Epifenomenalism, Huxley, Consciousness, Materialism, Evolution

results.title: 11.Intencionalidade de Brentano
results.summary: Brentano's thesis of intentionality defines mental phenomena by their directedness toward an object, distinguishing them from physical phenomena. This concept remains a central challenge in cognitive science, as it questions how physical systems can represent or point to external objects.
results.keywords: Intentionality, Brentano, Philosophy of Mind, Representation, Cognitive Science

results.title: 12.Funcionalismo Primitivo de William James
results.summary: William James's early functionalism introduced the concept of the 'stream of consciousness' and argued that mental states serve an active biological function. This pragmatic approach laid the groundwork for modern psychology and the later development of computational functionalism.
results.keywords: William James, Functionalism, Consciousness, Pragmatism, Philosophy of Mind

results.title: 13.Behaviorismo Logico
results.summary: Logical behaviorism, championed by Gilbert Ryle, argues that mental states are merely dispositions to behave in observable ways. This approach seeks to resolve Cartesian dualism by treating 'mind' as a category error, though it ultimately fails to account for subjective experience.
results.keywords: Logical Behaviorism, Gilbert Ryle, Category Error, Philosophy of Mind

results.title: 14.Teoria da Identidade de Tipos
results.summary: Type Identity Theory identifies mental states with specific brain states, using Frege's sense-reference distinction to explain their apparent difference. Despite its simplicity, the theory's rigidity regarding physical instantiation makes it unsuitable for flexible, cross-platform computational systems.
results.keywords: Type Identity, Materialism, Frege, Philosophy of Mind, Identity Theory

results.title: 15.Teoria da Identidade de Tipos - Argumentos
results.summary: Type Identity Theory argues that mental states are identical to neurophysiological brain states, offering a materialist reduction. However, the theory is undermined by the argument of multiple realizability, which demonstrates that mental functions can be instantiated in non-biological substrates.
results.keywords: Type Identity, Materialism, Multiple Realizability, Philosophy of Mind
results.path: Desenvolvimento_Histórico/15.Teoria da Identidade de Tipos - Argumentos.md

results.title: 16.Funcionalismo Computacional
results.summary: Computational functionalism posits that the mind is a system of symbol processing, analogous to software running on hardware. While this provides a robust framework for knowledge engineering, it faces significant challenges regarding subjective experience and the generation of genuine semantic understanding.
results.keywords: Computational Functionalism, Philosophy of Mind, Symbol Processing, Qualia, Searle

results.title: 16.Semiótica Computacional e Ontologias
results.summary: This note details the application of the 'Triangle of Meaning' to computational ontologies, emphasizing the distinction between stable kinds and contingent roles. It warns against modeling errors that confuse essential identity with operational context, which can lead to system rigidity.
results.keywords: Ontology, RDF, OWL, Semiotics, UFO, Knowledge Modeling

results.title: 17.Transicao Identidade para Funcionalismo
results.summary: The transition from Type Identity Theory to Functionalism reflects the shift toward multiple realizability in cognitive science and software architecture. By defining mental states through their functional roles rather than their physical makeup, the system allows for abstract models to be implemented across diverse hardware.
results.keywords: Functionalism, Multiple Realizability, Type Identity, Philosophy of Mind, Abstraction

results.title: 18.Frege e a Objetividade do Significado
results.summary: Frege's 'Third Realm' provides the philosophical justification for the Noosphera's goal of preserving objective meaning independent of physical or psychological support. This framework asserts that thoughts exist as objective, timeless entities that remain identical regardless of the language or medium used to express them.
results.keywords: Frege, Third Realm, Semantics, Objectivity, Philosophy of Language
results.path: Desenvolvimento_Histórico/18.Frege e a Objetividade do Significado.md

results.title: 19.Isomorfismo Estrutural e Invariancia
results.summary: Structural isomorphism is presented as the core mechanism for preserving meaning across different representational formats. By focusing on the integrity of relational topologies rather than individual data nodes, the system ensures that semantic identity remains invariant during technological migrations.
results.keywords: Isomorphism, Invariance, Semantics, Topology, Knowledge Representation

results.title: 2.Material Constitution
results.summary: This note examines the puzzles of material constitution, such as the relationship between a statue and the clay that forms it. It evaluates whether constitution implies identity or if they are distinct entities.
results.keywords: material constitution, identity, mereology, metaphysics

results.title: 2.Ocasionalismo de Malebranche
results.summary: Malebranche's occasionalism addresses the Cartesian interaction problem by proposing that no created substance has causal power. Instead, God acts as the sole efficient cause, intervening to produce physical or mental effects on the occasion of corresponding events in the other realm.
results.keywords: Occasionalism, Malebranche, Causality, Cartesianism, Philosophy of Mind

results.title: 20.Possiveis Abordagens e Horizontes a Desbravar
results.summary: This document outlines the theoretical foundations required to maintain identity across transformations, focusing on Type Theory, Category Theory, and Foundational Ontologies. It emphasizes using mathematical rigor to ensure that semantic structures remain invariant when migrated between different technological substrates.
results.keywords: Type Theory, Category Theory, HoTT, Semiotics, Foundational Ontology, Noosphera
results.path: Desenvolvimento_Histórico/20.Possiveis Abordagens e Horizontes a Desbravar.md

results.title: 21.A Polissemia e a Topologia do Significado
results.summary: This note explores polysemy through the lens of structuralist topology, arguing that meaning emerges from the relational neighborhood of symbols rather than intrinsic definitions. By anchoring symbols within specific topological graphs, the system stabilizes meaning and ensures consistency across different contexts.
results.keywords: Polysemy, Topology, Semiotics, Structuralism, Relational Meaning, Noosphera
results.path: Desenvolvimento_Histórico/21.A Polissemia e a Topologia do Significado.md

results.title: 22.O Funcionalismo e a Independência do Substrato no Noosphera
results.summary: The Noosphera project adopts functionalism to ensure that conceptual structures remain independent of their physical storage medium. By prioritizing functional and topological dynamics over hardware-specific implementations, the system achieves substrate independence and prevents semantic flattening.
results.keywords: Functionalism, Substrate Independence, Noosphera, Computational Philosophy, Ontology
results.path: Desenvolvimento_Histórico/22.O Funcionalismo e a Independência do Substrato no Noosphera.md

results.title: 3.Paralelismo de Spinoza
results.summary: Spinoza's monism rejects Cartesian dualism by positing that mind and body are not separate substances but two parallel attributes of a single infinite substance. This framework eliminates the interaction problem by suggesting that mental and physical events run in absolute synchronization without direct causal influence between them.
results.keywords: Spinoza, Monism, Psychophysical Parallelism, Substance, Descartes, Philosophy of Mind

results.title: Argumento Modal pela Necessidade das Identidades
results.summary: The modal argument for the necessity of identity proves that if two things are identical, they are necessarily identical. This provides the logical basis for the invariance of a KnowledgeObject's ID.
results.keywords: modal argument, necessity, identity, kripke

results.title: Aristóteles
results.summary: Aristotle was an ancient Greek philosopher who founded the Lyceum and established the foundations of Western logic and metaphysics. His hylomorphic theory distinguishes between matter and form, providing a framework for understanding change and identity.
results.keywords: Hylomorphism, Matter and Form, Essentialism, Metaphysics

results.title: Caminho-K
results.summary: A K-path is a formal element that, when combined with matter, constitutes a common object, acting as an organizing principle. It is analogous to the type and laws that define the structure of a KnowledgeObject independently of its payload.
results.keywords: k-path, hylomorphism, form and matter, identity

results.title: Conceitos Sortais
results.summary: Sortal concepts provide criteria for counting and identifying objects. The note explains how the Noösphera uses types as sortals to manage the identity and classification of KnowledgeObjects.
results.keywords: Sortal Concepts, Identity, Ontology, Noösphera, Classification

results.title: Constituição
results.summary: Constitution is the non-identical, non-symmetric relation between an object and its material components. It distinguishes the identity of a KnowledgeObject from its mutable payload, allowing for evolution without loss of essence.
results.keywords: constitution, identity, material composition, metaphysics

results.title: Critério de Identidade
results.summary: A criterion of identity provides the conditions necessary to determine if two occurrences are the same object. The note identifies the unique ID as the primary criterion for the Noösphera system.
results.keywords: Criterion of Identity, Identity, Metaphysics, Noösphera, Ontology

results.title: David Lewis
results.summary: David Lewis was a major 20th-century metaphysician who championed four-dimensionalism and modal realism. He proposed that objects persist through time by having temporal parts, providing a robust solution to the problem of temporary intrinsics.
results.keywords: Four-Dimensionalism, Perdurantism, Temporal Parts, Modal Realism

results.title: Denis Robinson
results.summary: Denis Robinson is a contemporary philosopher whose work focuses on identity and coincidence. He is noted for his observations on the qualitative indistinguishability of objects that occupy the same space, challenging traditional views on identity.
results.keywords: Coincidence, Qualitative Identity, Metaphysics, Identity

results.title: Doutrina das Partes Arbitrárias sem Anexo
results.summary: The Doctrine of Arbitrary Undetached Parts rejects the idea that every conceptual division of an object corresponds to a real part. This prevents ontological inflation in the Noösphera by ensuring only explicitly defined representations are treated as distinct entities.
results.keywords: arbitrary undetached parts, mereology, ontology, van Inwagen

results.title: Edmund Husserl
results.summary: Edmund Husserl was the founder of phenomenology, a philosophical movement focused on the structure of experience and consciousness. His work explores how objects are constituted in the mind through intentional acts.
results.keywords: Phenomenology, Consciousness, Intentionality, Epistemology

results.title: Edward Jonathan Lowe
results.summary: E. J. Lowe was a significant 20th-century metaphysician who defended non-Cartesian substance dualism and treated metaphysics as an autonomous discipline. He contributed to the debate on temporary intrinsics by proposing the use of tensed propositions.
results.keywords: Tensed Propositions, Substance Dualism, Metaphysics, Ontology

results.title: Entia Successiva
results.summary: Entia successiva are logical constructions composed of a succession of parts that replace one another over time. This concept models the historical sequence of representations that constitute the life of a KnowledgeObject.
results.keywords: entia successiva, successive entities, logical construction, persistence

results.title: Essential vs. Accidental Properties
results.summary: This note explores the distinction between essential and accidental properties, focusing on modal and 'whatness' senses. It discusses how these properties define an object's identity and essence.
results.keywords: essential properties, accidental properties, essence, metaphysics

results.title: Evolução da Modelagem Conceitual
results.summary: This note traces the evolution of conceptual modeling from hierarchical models to modern ontologies. It highlights the shift toward capturing semantics and enabling logical inference in information systems.
results.keywords: conceptual modeling, database evolution, semantics, ontologies
results.path: Topologia Epistemológica/Prof. Palazzo/Evolução da Modelagem Conceitual.md

results.title: Exdurantismo
results.summary: Exdurantism, or Stage Theory, posits that objects are instantaneous stages related by counterpart relations rather than 4D worms. This perspective allows the Noösphera to treat each representation as a temporal stage of a KnowledgeObject.
results.keywords: exdurantism, stage theory, four-dimensionalism, counterpart theory

results.title: Fissão
results.summary: Fission is the process of an entity splitting into multiple descendants, creating challenges for identity preservation. The Noösphera uses historical observations to track these branches while maintaining distinct identities for each new object.
results.keywords: fission, identity, branching, history

results.title: Fissão Assimétrica
results.summary: Asymmetric fission involves a split where descendants have different claims to the original identity based on form or matter. The Noösphera resolves this by prioritizing the ID as the primary marker of the original entity.
results.keywords: asymmetric fission, identity, ship of theseus, persistence

results.title: Fissão Simétrica
results.summary: Symmetric fission occurs when an entity splits into two identical descendants, both claiming the original identity. The Noösphera handles this by creating new IDs and documenting the bifurcation in the historical record.
results.keywords: symmetric fission, identity, bifurcation, genealogy

results.title: Forma (Filosofia)
results.summary: Form is the structural principle that defines an object's essence and identity. The note explains how the Noösphera uses form to maintain the stability of KnowledgeObjects despite changes in their content.
results.keywords: Form, Essence, Identity, Ontology, Noösphera

results.title: FOUNDATIONS
results.summary: This note acts as a foundational link for the Noosphera specification, pointing to the manifesto and the method of governance.
results.keywords: Noosphera, foundations, manifesto, governance

results.title: Frank Jackson
results.summary: Frank Jackson is a prominent philosopher of mind and metaphysics known for his 'Knowledge Argument' and his critique of four-dimensionalism. He introduced the 'shimmering universe' argument, warning against metaphysical theories that imply constant material renewal.
results.keywords: Four-Dimensionalism, Shimmering Universe, Metaphysics, Philosophy of Mind

results.title: Fundamentação (Grounding)
results.summary: Grounding is a metaphysical relation of ontological dependence that explains how higher-level facts are determined by more basic ones. It justifies why a KnowledgeObject's identity remains stable even when its material representations change.
results.keywords: grounding, ontological dependence, metaphysics, facts

results.title: Fusão
results.summary: Fusion is the process where two distinct entities merge into one, challenging the transitivity of identity. In the Noösphera, this is managed by creating a new KnowledgeObject and recording the genealogical history through observations.
results.keywords: fusion, fission, identity, genealogy

results.title: Harold Noonan
results.summary: Harold Noonan is a contemporary philosopher who challenges the distinction between constitution and identity. He argues that constitution is identity, critiquing the view that multiple objects can occupy the same space simultaneously.
results.keywords: Constitution, Identity, Spatial Coincidence, Metaphysics

results.title: Hilomorfismo
results.summary: Hylomorphism is the doctrine that substances are composed of matter and form. The note applies this to the Noösphera, where the payload is matter and the type/laws are the form.
results.keywords: Hylomorphism, Matter, Form, Ontology, Noösphera

results.title: Husserl - Investigações Lógicas VI
results.summary: Husserl's Sixth Logical Investigation explores the phenomenological basis of knowledge, distinguishing between empty intentions and intuitive fulfillment. This work provides a foundation for the Noosphera's architecture, specifically regarding the relationship between theoretical representations and empirical observations.
results.keywords: Husserl, Phenomenology, Epistemology, Knowledge Representation, Noosphera

results.title: Identidade
results.summary: Identity is the relation of self-sameness, representing the central problem of metaphysics. The note details how the Noösphera architecture maintains identity through formal laws and structural constraints.
results.keywords: Identity, Metaphysics, Persistence, Noösphera, Ontology

results.title: Identidade Diacrônica
results.summary: Diachronic identity is the persistence of an object through time. The note details how the Noösphera ensures this persistence through historical records and identity invariance.
results.keywords: Diachronic Identity, Persistence, Metaphysics, Noösphera, Ontology

results.title: Identidade dos Indiscerníveis
results.summary: The Identity of Indiscernibles states that objects sharing all properties are identical. The note clarifies that the Noösphera does not adopt this principle, distinguishing between qualitative similarity and numerical identity.
results.keywords: Identity of Indiscernibles, Leibniz, Identity, Logic, Noösphera

results.title: Identidade Estrita
results.summary: Strict identity is the rigorous philosophical requirement that two objects are identical only if they share all their parts. In the Noösphera architecture, this defines the invariant essence of a KnowledgeObject, such as its ID and type, distinguishing it from its mutable payload.
results.keywords: strict identity, identity, essence, invariance

results.title: Identidade Frouxa
results.summary: Loose identity describes the common-sense notion that an object can change its parts while remaining the same entity over time. It is essential for tracking the evolution of a KnowledgeObject as its payload changes while maintaining its unique identifier.
results.keywords: loose identity, persistence, entia successiva, identity over time

results.title: Identidade Numérica
results.summary: Numerical identity is the relation of being the same object, anchored by a unique identifier. The note explains its role as the primary criterion for identity in the Noösphera architecture.
results.keywords: Numerical Identity, Identity, Metaphysics, Noösphera, Ontology

results.title: Identidade Qualitativa
results.summary: Qualitative identity refers to the exact resemblance of properties between two objects. The note distinguishes this from numerical identity, which is the core of the Noösphera's object tracking.
results.keywords: Qualitative Identity, Similarity, Identity, Metaphysics, Noösphera

results.title: Identidade Relativa
results.summary: Relative identity suggests that identity is dependent on the sortal or type of the object. The note explores how this concept informs the Noösphera's approach to object classification and identity.
results.keywords: Relative Identity, Sortals, Metaphysics, Noösphera, Ontology

results.title: Identidade Sincrônica
results.summary: Synchronic identity refers to the identity of an object at a single moment in time. The note describes its role in validating the consistency of KnowledgeObjects within the Noösphera.
results.keywords: Synchronic Identity, Identity, Metaphysics, Noösphera, Logic

results.title: Identidade Temporária
results.summary: Temporary identity is the thesis that objects can be identical at one time and distinct at another. The note explains why the Noösphera generally rejects this in favor of invariant identity.
results.keywords: Temporary Identity, Metaphysics, Persistence, Noösphera, Logic

results.title: Identidades Contingentes
results.summary: Contingent identities suggest that identity can vary across possible worlds, a view largely rejected in favor of necessary identity. The Noösphera treats the identity of a KnowledgeObject as a necessary, invariant property.
results.keywords: contingent identity, necessary identity, kripke, metaphysics

results.title: Identidades Indeterminadas
results.summary: Indeterminate identities suggest that it can be vague whether two things are identical. The Noösphera rejects this, adhering to the principle that identity must be binary and determined to ensure system coherence.
results.keywords: indeterminate identity, vagueness, logic, bivalence

results.title: Identity
results.summary: This note provides a comprehensive overview of identity in philosophy, covering criteria of identity, identity over time, and the debate between perdurance and endurance. It also addresses the radical view that identity is relative rather than absolute.
results.keywords: identity, personal identity, persistence, metaphysics

results.title: Identity Over Time-nota
results.summary: This note examines the diachronic identity paradox, where an object's change challenges its numerical identity. It discusses classical solutions like Aristotelian hylomorphism and modern approaches like four-dimensionalism.
results.keywords: diachronic identity, hylomorphism, four-dimensionalism, Leibniz's Law

results.title: Identity Over Time-reflexão
results.summary: This note explores the philosophical paradox of identity over time, contrasting the concept of 'Absolute Identity' with 'Continuous Change'. It highlights the Noosphera project's architectural approach to separating immutable identity from transient states.
results.keywords: identity, change, Noosphera, ontology, Leibniz's Law

results.title: Indiscernibilidade dos Idênticos
results.summary: The Indiscernibility of Identicals, or Leibniz's Law, states that identical objects must share all properties. This principle serves as the logical foundation for the Noösphera's Law of Identity Invariance.
results.keywords: Leibniz's Law, Identity, Logic, Indiscernibility, Noösphera

results.title: Instanciação (Relação)
results.summary: Triadic instantiation proposes that properties are instantiated by objects in relation to time. This allows the Noösphera to track the evolution of a KnowledgeObject by linking its payload to a specific timestamp.
results.keywords: triadic instantiation, properties, time, persistence

results.title: Intenção Significativa
results.summary: Meaning-intention refers to the act of aiming at a concept without the immediate presence of its empirical object. This concept highlights the autonomy of semantic structures, which maintain identity and validity even before they are instantiated or observed.
results.keywords: Meaning-Intention, Husserl, Semantics, Phenomenology, Noosphera

results.title: Intrínsecos Temporários
results.summary: Temporary intrinsics addresses how an object can have incompatible properties at different times. The Noösphera adopts a four-dimensionalist solution, treating each representation as a temporal part of the object's history.
results.keywords: temporary intrinsics, four-dimensionalism, persistence, change

results.title: Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic Properties
results.summary: This note distinguishes between intrinsic and extrinsic properties, analyzing how objects possess properties based on their internal nature versus their interactions. It highlights the difficulty of providing a precise analysis of this intuitive distinction.
results.keywords: intrinsic properties, extrinsic properties, metaphysics, properties

results.title: Justin Mooney
results.summary: Justin Mooney is a contemporary philosopher who has revived 'Phasalism,' the view that there are no substance sortals, only phase sortals. He suggests that objects are 'thin particulars' that acquire and lose properties without changing their underlying identity.
results.keywords: Phasalism, Thin Particular, Phase Sortals, Identity

results.title: Katherine Hawley
results.summary: Katherine Hawley is a contemporary philosopher who advocates for 'Exdurantism' or the Stage Theory of persistence. She posits that objects are instantaneous temporal stages, and persistence is a relation between these stages rather than an object spanning time as a whole.
results.keywords: Exdurantism, Stage Theory, Four-Dimensionalism, Persistence

results.title: Lei de Leibniz
results.summary: Leibniz's Law, or the Indiscernibility of Identicals, states that identical objects share all properties. This principle is the formal criterion for coherence in the Noösphera's identity management.
results.keywords: Leibniz's Law, Identity, Logic, Indiscernibility, Noösphera

results.title: Lei III — A Inerência da Observabilidade
results.summary: David Hume's bundle theory of the self challenges the notion of a permanent mental substance, arguing instead that the 'self' is merely a collection of fleeting perceptions. This empiricist perspective emphasizes memory and habit as the mechanisms creating the illusion of personal identity.
results.keywords: Hume, Bundle Theory, Personal Identity, Empiricism, Philosophy of Mind
results.path: Noosphera/01_CONCEPTUAL MODEL/03 — Leis e Invariantes/Matriz de Invariantes/Lei III — A Inerência da Observabilidade.md

results.title: Lei IV — A Exclusividade Cognitiva das Competências
results.summary: The Enlightenment mechanism movement, exemplified by La Mettrie, argued that humans are complex biological machines. This radical monism rejected the existence of an immaterial soul, framing mental states as direct consequences of physical and organic conditions.
results.keywords: Mecanicismo, Materialism, Enlightenment, Philosophy of Mind, Biological Machines
results.path: Noosphera/01_CONCEPTUAL MODEL/03 — Leis e Invariantes/Matriz de Invariantes/Lei IV — A Exclusividade Cognitiva das Competências.md

results.title: Lei IX — A Primazia da Ontologia sobre a Arquitetura
results.summary: Immanuel Kant's transcendental synthesis posits that the mind is an active structure that constructs reality through innate categories like time, space, and causality. This framework provides a middle ground between pure empiricism and rationalist dualism.
results.keywords: Kant, Transcendental Idealism, Cognitive Architecture, Epistemology, Philosophy of Mind
results.path: Noosphera/01_CONCEPTUAL MODEL/03 — Leis e Invariantes/Matriz de Invariantes/Lei IX — A Primazia da Ontologia sobre a Arquitetura.md

results.title: Lei V — A Autonomia das Competências
results.summary: Phrenology, while ultimately a pseudoscientific endeavor, introduced the crucial concept of localizing cognitive functions to specific brain regions. This shift from a unified soul to a fragmented, observable brain structure paved the way for modern neurology.
results.keywords: Phrenology, Localizacionismo, Neuroscience History, Brain Anatomy, Cognitive Functions
results.path: Noosphera/01_CONCEPTUAL MODEL/03 — Leis e Invariantes/Matriz de Invariantes/Lei V — A Autonomia das Competências.md

results.title: Lei VI — A Transitoriedade dos Estados
results.summary: The German Scientific Materialism movement of the 1850s sought to reduce all mental phenomena to physiological and chemical processes. This radical reductionism aimed to replace traditional metaphysics with empirical science, significantly impacting the development of modern psychology.
results.keywords: Materialism, Reductionism, 19th Century Science, Philosophy of Mind, Physiology
results.path: Noosphera/01_CONCEPTUAL MODEL/03 — Leis e Invariantes/Matriz de Invariantes/Lei VI — A Transitoriedade dos Estados.md

results.title: Lei VII — A Natureza Retrospectiva dos Eventos
results.summary: Gustav Fechner's psychophysics represents a landmark attempt to quantify mental sensations through mathematical laws. By establishing a logarithmic relationship between physical stimuli and mental perception, it bridged the gap between subjective experience and empirical science.
results.keywords: Psychophysics, Fechner, Weber-Fechner Law, Panpsychism, Experimental Psychology
results.path: Noosphera/01_CONCEPTUAL MODEL/03 — Leis e Invariantes/Matriz de Invariantes/Lei VII — A Natureza Retrospectiva dos Eventos.md

results.summary: This historiographical overview traces the evolution of the philosophy of mind from ancient Greek concepts of the soul to 19th-century materialist theories. It maps the shifting definitions of the 'self' and the mind-body problem across major philosophical eras.
results.keywords: Philosophy of Mind, History of Philosophy, Dualism, Materialism, Historiography
results.path: Noosphera/01_CONCEPTUAL MODEL/03 — Leis e Invariantes/Matriz de Invariantes/Lei VIII — A Neutralidade Semântica da Persistência.md

results.summary: The ontology document establishes the foundational entities of the Noosphera system, focusing on what exists independently of implementation. It categorizes entities into specific conceptual continents to ensure clear boundaries and maintainable system architecture.

results.summary: This note outlines the invariant laws that govern the Noosphera system, ensuring that fundamental principles remain true regardless of technological evolution. results.title: Mark Steen
results.summary: Mark Steen is a contemporary philosopher recognized for his meticulous exegesis of Roderick Chisholm's work on identity. His research provides a historical and critical foundation for understanding the evolution of Chisholm's metaphysical theories.
results.keywords: Roderick Chisholm, Identity, Metaphysics, Exegesis

results.title: Matéria (Filosofia)
results.summary: Matter is the indeterminate substratum that is organized by form to create a substance. In the Noösphera, matter represents the volatile payload that can change without altering the object's identity.
results.keywords: Matter, Hylomorphism, Ontology, Noösphera, Metaphysics

results.title: MATERIALIZATION
results.summary: This note links to the implementation and reference architecture layers of the Noosphera project.
results.keywords: Noosphera, materialization, implementation, architecture

results.title: Mereologia
results.summary: Mereology is the formal theory of parts and wholes, examining how objects are composed and how parts relate to the whole. It provides the logical foundation for understanding how a KnowledgeObject is constructed from its various representations and observations.
results.keywords: mereology, composition, parts and wholes, mereological sum, ontology

results.title: Mereologia Irrestrita
results.summary: Unrestricted mereology suggests that any collection of objects forms a valid whole, a principle the Noosphera explicitly rejects to prevent ontological inflation. Instead, the system uses formal grammar to define which compositions are valid, ensuring only meaningful structures are created.
results.keywords: Mereology, Ontology, Composition, Noosphera, Metaphysics

results.title: Michael Burke
results.summary: Michael Burke is a contemporary philosopher known for his 'Theory of Dominant Kinds' and his approach to the puzzle of coincident objects. He argues that objects can cease to exist when they lose their defining parts, representing a shift in ontological category.
results.keywords: Dominant Kinds, Arbitrary Undetached Parts, Ontology, Coincidence

results.title: Milton Munitz
results.summary: Milton Munitz was a 20th-century philosopher and editor who played a crucial role in organizing the debate on identity and individuation. His edited volumes helped consolidate key discussions on modal logic and necessity.
results.keywords: Identity, Individuation, Modal Logic, Philosophy of Science

results.title: Modelagem Conceitual
results.summary: This note discusses conceptual modeling as a cognitive process of translating human perception into formal structures. It emphasizes the challenge of aligning subjective knowledge with computational requirements.
results.keywords: conceptual modeling, perception, information systems, representation

results.title: Modificador Adverbial
results.summary: Adverbial modifiers suggest that temporal references modify the manner of property instantiation. This provides a useful analogy for how a KnowledgeObject manifests different payloads at different times without changing its essence.
results.keywords: adverbial modifier, temporal properties, instantiation, metaphysics

results.title: Mudança (Filosofia)
results.summary: Change is defined as the transition between states, posing a fundamental challenge to identity. The note discusses how the Noösphera manages change through a formal distinction between essential and accidental transformations.
results.keywords: Change, Philosophy, Identity, Metaphysics, Noösphera

results.title: Mudança Acidental
results.summary: Accidental change refers to transformations that do not affect an object's core identity. The note explains how the Noösphera architecture permits these changes to facilitate system evolution.
results.keywords: Accidental Change, Identity, Metaphysics, Noösphera, Ontology

results.title: Mudança Essencial
results.summary: Essential change involves the loss of core properties, leading to the destruction of an object's identity. The note outlines how the Noösphera system detects and manages such changes.
results.keywords: Essential Change, Identity, Metaphysics, Noösphera, Ontology

results.title: Navio de Teseu
results.summary: The Ship of Theseus is a classic paradox concerning identity through time when parts are replaced. It illustrates the tension between material and formal continuity, resolved in the Noösphera by viewing objects as 4D histories.
results.keywords: ship of theseus, paradox, identity, persistence

results.title: Noosphera_Especificacao_Completa
results.summary: This note provides the complete specification for the Noosphera project, focusing on preserving the identity of meaning across technological transformations. It establishes the normative hierarchy for the project.
results.keywords: Noosphera, meaning, identity, specification, governance

results.title: O que é Ontologia
results.summary: This note defines ontology in the context of computer science as a formal tool for conceptual modeling. It traces the evolution from philosophical categories to modern computational schemas.
results.keywords: ontology, conceptual modeling, taxonomy, logic
results.path: Topologia Epistemológica/Prof. Palazzo/O que é Ontologia.md

results.title: Ontologia - Conceitos
results.summary: This note details the use of ontologies in computer science for rigorous knowledge representation. It covers formal structures, logical inference, and the challenges of integrating different ontologies.
results.keywords: ontology, knowledge representation, inference, logic

results.title: Operador Sentencial
results.summary: Sentential operators treat temporal references as modifiers of entire propositions. This allows the Noösphera to evaluate the truth and coherence of representations relative to the specific time they were created.
results.keywords: sentential operator, temporal logic, truth, observations

results.title: Paradoxo da Mudança
results.summary: The Paradox of Change explores the tension between an object changing and remaining the same. The note presents this as the fundamental problem the Noösphera architecture is designed to solve.
results.keywords: Paradox of Change, Identity, Persistence, Metaphysics, Noösphera

results.title: Partes Temporais
results.summary: Temporal parts are segments of an object existing at different moments, central to the four-dimensionalist view of persistence. The note links these to the history of KnowledgeObjects in the Noösphera.
results.keywords: Temporal Parts, Four-dimensionalism, Persistence, Metaphysics, Noösphera

results.title: Perdurantismo
results.summary: Perdurantism views objects as four-dimensional entities composed of temporal parts, providing a robust framework for tracking object history. The Noosphera adopts this view, treating knowledge objects as continuous entities whose history is composed of successive representational stages.
results.keywords: Perdurantism, Quadridimensionalism, Ontology, Noosphera, Persistence

results.title: Perspectivalismo
results.summary: Perspectivalism allows for the evaluation of identity from multiple, non-contradictory viewpoints, such as the structural vs. the historical perspective. This approach enables the Noosphera to reconcile different ways of interpreting knowledge objects without sacrificing logical rigor.
results.keywords: Perspectivalism, Identity, Ontology, Noosphera, Metaphysics

results.title: Peter Geach
results.summary: Peter Geach was a 20th-century philosopher who defended the theory of 'Relative Identity.' He argued that identity is not an absolute relation but is always relative to a sortal concept, such as 'same statue' or 'same lump of clay.'
results.keywords: Relative Identity, Sortal Concepts, Logic, Philosophy of Language

results.title: Policy Contract
results.summary: This note serves as a conceptual index mapping the foundational layers of a formal system model. It outlines the hierarchical progression from passive ontology and invariant laws to the establishment of a formal grammar.
results.keywords: Ontology, Formal Grammar, System Modeling, Knowledge Representation, Conceptual Framework
results.path: Noosphera/02_ARCHITECTURE/06 — Engenharia de Design/Contratos de Materialização Arquitetural/Policy Contract.md

results.title: Preenchimento Fenomenológico
results.summary: Phenomenological fulfillment describes the synthesis where a conceptual intention is confirmed by intuitive evidence. In the Noosphera architecture, this maps to the transition where a theoretical structure is validated by empirical observation without altering the underlying ontology.
results.keywords: Phenomenology, Husserl, Fulfillment, Epistemology, Noosphera

results.title: Presentismo
results.summary: Presentism is the thesis that only the present exists, which the Noösphera rejects in favor of an eternalist view. By preserving the full historical record, the system ensures that the past remains as real and accessible as the present.
results.keywords: presentism, eternalism, time, history

results.title: Princípio da Superveniência
results.summary: The principle of supervenience asserts that higher-level properties are determined by basic physical facts. This principle underpins the Noosphera's architecture, ensuring that the identity of a knowledge object is always grounded in its fundamental representational and observational data.
results.keywords: Supervenience, Metaphysics, Ontology, Noosphera, Identity

results.title: Problema das Mentes Demais
results.summary: The problem of 'too many minds' challenges constitutionalist ontologies by suggesting that coincident objects share identical mental states. The Noosphera avoids this by enforcing strict coherence rules that prevent conflicting interpretations of the same knowledge object.
results.keywords: Too Many Minds, Ontology, Metaphysics, Noosphera, Coherence

results.title: Problema dos Intrínsecos Temporários
results.summary: Note is empty or too short for semantic analysis (0 chars)

results.title: Proposições Tencionadas
results.summary: Tensed propositions include intrinsic temporal references, allowing for the expression of facts about the past, present, and future. These are essential for indexing observations to specific times within the Noösphera.
results.keywords: tensed propositions, temporal logic, time, observations

results.title: Propriedades Acidentais
results.summary: Accidental properties are contingent characteristics that can change without affecting an object's identity. The note explains how these properties allow for flexible versioning and evolution within the Noösphera.
results.keywords: Accidental Properties, Contingency, Identity, Metaphysics, Noösphera

results.title: Propriedades Essenciais
results.summary: Essential properties are those that define an object's identity, and their loss results in the destruction of that identity. The note discusses how the Noösphera architecture protects these properties to maintain system coherence.
results.keywords: Essential Properties, Essence, Identity, Metaphysics, Noösphera

results.title: Propriedades Extrínsecas
results.summary: Extrinsic properties are defined as characteristics dependent on an object's relations to other entities or its environment. The note explains how these properties allow for dynamic changes in the Noösphera system without compromising the object's core identity.
results.keywords: Extrinsic Properties, Relations, Metaphysics, Noösphera, Ontology

results.title: Propriedades Intrínsecas
results.summary: Intrinsic properties are defined as characteristics an object possesses independently of its environment or relations. The note discusses their role in the Noösphera architecture as inviolable markers of an object's identity.
results.keywords: Intrinsic Properties, Metaphysics, Identity, Noösphera, Ontology

results.title: Propriedades Modais
results.summary: Modal properties express necessity or possibility, distinguishing between what is essential and what is contingent. The note explains how these properties are used in the Noösphera to enforce structural integrity.
results.keywords: Modal Properties, Necessity, Possibility, Logic, Noösphera

results.title: Quadridimensionalismo
results.summary: Four-dimensionalism posits that objects are extended in both space and time, consisting of temporal parts. This framework provides the ontological basis for how KnowledgeObjects persist and evolve within the Noösphera.
results.keywords: Four-dimensionalism, Temporal Parts, Persistence, Metaphysics, Noösphera

results.title: Reflexividade
results.summary: Reflexivity is defined as a binary relation property where every element relates to itself, forming a core component of equivalence relations. The note explains its role in ensuring that every KnowledgeObject in the Noösphera system is identical to itself.
results.keywords: Reflexivity, Identity, Equivalence Relation, Logic, Noösphera

results.title: Relação de Equivalência
results.summary: An equivalence relation is a binary relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Identity is the fundamental equivalence relation, ensuring the logical consistency of KnowledgeObject references.
results.keywords: equivalence relation, identity, logic, reflexivity

results.title: Relative Identity
results.summary: This note analyzes the concept of relative identity, which challenges the standard view of absolute identity. It explores how objects can be the same under one kind but distinct under another.
results.keywords: relative identity, absolute identity, Peter Geach, metaphysics

results.title: Réplica (Fasalismo)
results.summary: In the context of fasalism, a replica is a reconstructed object that lacks identity with the original due to a lack of historical continuity. The Noosphera applies this to ensure that reconstructed data objects are only treated as the original if historical continuity is explicitly maintained.
results.keywords: Replica, Fasalism, Identity, Continuity, Noosphera

results.title: Representation Contract
results.summary: This note defines the Architecture layer as the bridge between formal grammar and technological implementation, focusing on the creation of processes that enable system events. It establishes four core functional roles—Persistence, Cognition, Orchestration, and Governance—to ensure that system components remain modular, independent, and strictly aligned with ontological laws.
results.keywords: System Architecture, Functional Decomposition, Architectural Patterns, Component Design, Process Orchestration
results.path: Noosphera/02_ARCHITECTURE/06 — Engenharia de Design/Contratos de Materialização Arquitetural/Representation Contract.md

results.title: Roderick Chisholm
results.summary: Roderick Chisholm was a 20th-century philosopher who made significant contributions to metaphysics and epistemology, particularly regarding identity through time. He proposed a distinction between strict identity, which requires identical parts, and loose identity, which accounts for objects changing over time.
results.keywords: Strict Identity, Loose Identity, Entia Successiva, Metaphysics, Epistemology

results.title: Runtime Context Contract
results.summary: This note details the Engineering Design layer, which translates architectural responsibilities into technology-agnostic contracts and structural patterns. It emphasizes that infrastructure must remain passive and subordinate to domain logic, ensuring that software construction preserves established architectural boundaries and invariants.
results.keywords: Software Engineering, Design Contracts, Dependency Inversion, Architectural Boundaries, Domain-Driven Design
results.path: Noosphera/02_ARCHITECTURE/06 — Engenharia de Design/Contratos de Sustentação Arquitetural/Runtime Context Contract.md

results.title: Sally Haslanger
results.summary: Sally Haslanger is a contemporary philosopher whose work spans analytic metaphysics, social ontology, and feminist theory. She has contributed to the debate on temporary intrinsics by advocating for the use of tensed propositions.
results.keywords: Social Ontology, Tensed Propositions, Feminist Philosophy, Metaphysics

results.title: Saul Kripke
results.summary: Saul Kripke was a foundational figure in 20th-century logic and philosophy of language, famous for his work on modal logic and naming. He argued that identity is necessary and that proper names are rigid designators.
results.keywords: Rigid Designators, Modal Logic, Necessary Identity, Naming and Necessity

results.title: Semiótica e Representação
results.summary: This note explains the application of semiotics to computer science, focusing on the mapping between reality, mental models, and formal symbols. It emphasizes the importance of semantics in data modeling.
results.keywords: semiotics, semantics, representation, ontology, RDF

results.title: Simetria
results.summary: This note defines symmetry as a binary relation property where if aRb, then bRa, serving as a pillar for equivalence relations. It highlights the necessity of symmetry for identity in the Noösphera architecture to ensure logical coherence.
results.keywords: Symmetry, Identity, Equivalence Relation, Logic, Noösphera

results.title: Sobredeterminação Causal
results.summary: Causal overdetermination serves as a critical warning for ontological design, highlighting the risk of attributing multiple causes to a single effect when distinguishing between form and matter. The Noosphera mitigates this by enforcing a single validation mechanism for state changes.
results.keywords: Causal Overdetermination, Ontology, Metaphysics, Noosphera, Causality

results.title: Sortais de Fase
results.summary: Phase sortals describe transient states or properties that an object can lose while maintaining its existence. The note contrasts these with substance sortals and applies them to the format of representations in the Noösphera.
results.keywords: Phase Sortals, Identity, Metaphysics, Noösphera, Ontology

results.title: Sortais de Substância
results.summary: Substance sortals define the essential categories that an object cannot lose without ceasing to exist. The note explains how the 'type' of a KnowledgeObject functions as a substance sortal in the Noösphera architecture.
results.keywords: Substance Sortals, Essence, Identity, Ontology, Noösphera

results.title: Temporal Parts
results.summary: This note discusses the metaphysical concept of temporal parts, where objects persist through time by having slices at different moments. It evaluates the debate between perdurance and endurance theories.
results.keywords: temporal parts, perdurance, endurance, metaphysics

results.title: Teoria da Correspondência da Verdade
results.summary: The correspondence theory of truth states that a proposition is true if it corresponds to a fact. This is applied in the Noösphera to validate observations as true records of events that occurred within the system.
results.keywords: correspondence theory, truth, facts, observations

results.title: Teoria dos Correspondentes
results.summary: Counterpart theory addresses modal properties by suggesting that objects in different possible worlds are counterparts rather than identical entities. This concept is applied in the Noosphera to manage different versions or representations of a knowledge object as related counterparts.
results.keywords: Counterpart Theory, David Lewis, Modality, Ontology, Noosphera

results.title: Teoria dos Estágios
results.summary: Stage Theory, or exdurantism, posits that objects are instantaneous temporal parts related by counterpart relations rather than continuous 4D worms. This framework offers an alternative way to model object persistence in the Noosphera by treating versions as stages of a single knowledge object.
results.keywords: Stage Theory, Exdurantism, Persistence, Ontology, Noosphera

results.title: The Identity of Indiscernibles
results.summary: This note defines the Identity of Indiscernibles, the metaphysical thesis that numerical difference requires qualitative difference. It explores the principle's axiomatic nature and its influence on identity theory.
results.keywords: identity, indiscernibles, Leibniz, metaphysics

results.title: Thomson
results.summary: Judith Jarvis Thomson was a prominent philosopher known for her work in metaphysics and law, particularly her defense of the 'Coincidence View.' She argued that distinct objects can occupy the same space at the same time.
results.keywords: Coincidence View, Spatial Coincidence, Metaphysics, Philosophy of Law

results.title: Time Travel
results.summary: This note provides an overview of philosophical and physical perspectives on time travel. It covers logical paradoxes, causation, and the metaphysics of change.
results.keywords: time travel, Grandfather paradox, causation, metaphysics

results.title: Transitividade
results.summary: Transitivity is the property where a relation holds between a and c if it holds between a and b, and b and c. It is a cornerstone of identity, ensuring that the Noösphera maintains a consistent and logical knowledge graph.
results.keywords: transitivity, identity, logic, equivalence

results.title: Transitividade da Identidade
results.summary: Transitivity of identity is the logical property where if a equals b and b equals c, then a equals c. This property is vital for maintaining the coherence of the knowledge graph and ensuring identity chains remain unbroken.
results.keywords: transitivity, identity, equivalence relation, logic

results.title: Transitividade da Identidade Temporária (TTI)
results.summary: Temporary Identity Transitivity (TTI) is a relativistic approach to identity that preserves transitiveness within specific timeframes. While useful in some metaphysical contexts, the Noosphera rejects this in favor of absolute identity to ensure historical traceability and logical consistency.
results.keywords: TTI, Identity, Metaphysics, Transitiveness, Noosphera

results.title: Type Theory in Computer Science, Linguistic, Logic
results.summary: This note serves as a placeholder for exploring Type Theory in computer science, linguistics, and logic. It aims to define the foundational concepts of type systems.
results.keywords: type theory, logic, computer science, linguistics
results.path: Topologia Epistemológica/Attic/Type Theory in Computer Science, Linguistic, Logic.md

results.title: Visão Relacional
results.summary: The relational view attempts to solve temporal problems by treating intrinsic properties as relations to time. The Noösphera uses this concept to model payloads as relations between objects, formats, and timestamps.
results.keywords: relational view, temporal properties, metaphysics, payload

results.title: Wittgenstein
results.summary: Ludwig Wittgenstein was a highly influential 20th-century philosopher who explored the limits of language and logic. His early work questioned the necessity of identity, while his later work focused on language games and the social nature of meaning.
results.keywords: Language Games, Tractatus, Philosophy of Language, Logic
